statement:
Let u:C→D be **continuous and cocontinuous** as a functor of sites, with associated morphism g:Sh(C)→Sh(D). This supports lower shriek g_! left adjoint to inverse image g^{-1}; for a ring sheaf O_D, set O_C=g^{-1}O_D so the module inverse image g^* agrees with g^{-1}. This is a named setup **only in candidates explicitly assuming these properties**. Without the additional fibre-product preservation hypothesis, module and abelian-sheaf derived lower shriek need not commute with forgetting (source warning lines 9435–9468).

Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a continuous and cocontinuous
functor of sites. Let $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be the corresponding morphism of topoi. Let $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$
be a sheaf of rings and let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$-module. Then
$H^p(U, g^{-1}\mathcal{I}) = 0$ for all $p > 0$ and $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
hypotheses: u:C→D is continuous and cocontinuous and g is the associated morphism of topoi.
O_D is a sheaf of rings and I an injective O_D-module.
conclusions: For every site object U∈C and every p>0, H^p(U,g^{-1}I)=0 (underlying abelian cohomology).

statement:
Let u:C→D be **continuous and cocontinuous** as a functor of sites, with associated morphism g:Sh(C)→Sh(D). This supports lower shriek g_! left adjoint to inverse image g^{-1}; for a ring sheaf O_D, set O_C=g^{-1}O_D so the module inverse image g^* agrees with g^{-1}. This is a named setup **only in candidates explicitly assuming these properties**. Without the additional fibre-product preservation hypothesis, module and abelian-sheaf derived lower shriek need not commute with forgetting (source warning lines 9435–9468). The two clauses have **separate coefficient categories**: (1) arbitrary derived abelian sheaf M∈D(D), with inverse image g^{-1}; (2) module-derived M∈D(O_D) when O_C=g^{-1}O_D, with pullback g^*. These should not be conflated.

Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a continuous and cocontinuous
functor of sites. Let $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be the corresponding morphism of topoi. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $M$ in $D(\mathcal{D})$ we have
$R\Gamma(U, g^{-1}M) = R\Gamma(u(U), M)$.
\item If $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$ is a sheaf of rings and
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C} = g^{-1}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$, then
for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ we have
$R\Gamma(U, g^*M) = R\Gamma(u(U), M)$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: u:C→D is continuous and cocontinuous and g is the induced topos morphism.
U∈C; for the module clause O_D is a ring sheaf and O_C=g^{-1}O_D.
conclusions: For every M∈D(Ab(D)), there is an isomorphism RΓ(U,g^{-1}M)≅RΓ(u(U),M).
For every M∈D(O_D), RΓ(U,g^*M)≅RΓ(u(U),M), with the rings as specified.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-pullback-same-cohomology}
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a continuous and cocontinuous
functor of sites. Let $g : \Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be the corresponding morphism of topoi. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For $M$ in $D(\mathcal{D})$ we have
$R\Gamma(U, g^{-1}M) = R\Gamma(u(U), M)$.
\item If $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$ is a sheaf of rings and
$\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C} = g^{-1}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D}$, then
for $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ we have
$R\Gamma(U, g^*M) = R\Gamma(u(U), M)$.
\end{enumerate}
